organism_context: Ralstonia sp. PS12 and other chloroaromatic degraders using the modified ortho-cleavage (chlorocatechol) pathway
rationale: The chlorolactone/chloromuconate interconversion of the 3,4-dichlorotoluene chlorocatechol pathway is run by a chloromuconate cycloisomerase (EC 5.5.1.7), an Mn2+-dependent homooctameric enolase-superfamily protein with a single cycloisomerase active site. The accompanying chloride elimination is spontaneous chemistry on the cycloisomerization product, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Physiological catabolic flux is cycloisomerization (dichloromethylmuconate -> chlorolactone), made effectively irreversible by spontaneous chloride elimination from the product, so the LLM's '<' matches biology; ModelSEED's '>' simply follows the IUBMB systematic name, which writes the enzyme as a ring-opening lyase.

enzyme_name: unidentified NADP-coupled oxidoreductase of an acyl-tetronate / butenolide pathway
rationale: MetaCyc RXN1UA-50 is an organism-specific entry I could not resolve (biocyc.org was unreachable from this environment) and the reaction carries no EC, KEGG or Rhea cross-reference. The chemistry is an NADP+-coupled desaturation of a 4-octanoyl-butyrolactone methyl phosphate to the corresponding butenolide, consistent with an acyl-tetronate natural-product pathway, but no catalysing protein could be confirmed.
direction_note: In a tetronate/butenolide biosynthetic route the desaturation (left-to-right as written) would be the productive direction, favouring ModelSEED's '>', but with the enzyme unidentified this is not firm.

enzyme_name: unidentified benzylisoquinoline-alkaloid N-demethylase of the papaverine pathway (or coclaurine/tetrahydropapaverine N-methyltransferase CNMT running in reverse)
organism_context: Papaver somniferum (opium poppy), MetaCyc PWY-7363 papaverine biosynthesis
rationale: The laudanosine / (S)-tetrahydropapaverine step is an N-methyl transfer, and no N-demethylase has been characterised for it in opium poppy; the alkaloid N-demethylases described to date are heterologous/engineered systems rather than the poppy enzyme. ModelSEED's record has had all cofactors stripped, so it cannot be distinguished from the SAM-dependent N-methyltransferase running backwards.
direction_note: If the underlying step is the SAM-dependent N-methylation (CNMT) with SAM/SAH stripped out, the physiological direction is tetrahydropapaverine -> laudanosine, i.e. the LLM's '<'; a genuine oxidative N-demethylation would instead be irreversible in ModelSEED's '>' direction.

organism_context: Ralstonia eutropha JMP134 / Pseudomonas spp. degrading 1,4-dichlorobenzene via 3,6-dichlorocatechol and 2,5-dichloro-cis,cis-muconate
rationale: The 2,5-dichloromuconate / chlorolactone couple of the chlorocatechol ortho pathway is handled by chloromuconate cycloisomerase (EC 5.5.1.7, TfdD/ClcB), a single-activity Mn2+-dependent enolase-superfamily cycloisomerase that assembles as a homooctamer of one chain. Its dehalogenating behaviour is a consequence of the same cycloisomerization active site, not a second fused activity.
direction_note: The catabolic direction in vivo is cycloisomerization (muconate -> chlorolactone, then spontaneous chloride loss), i.e. the LLM's '<'; ModelSEED's '>' reflects the IUBMB ring-opening-lyase naming convention rather than pathway flux.

organism_context: Flavobacteriia/Bacteroidetes flexixanthin producers (e.g. Algoriphagus spp., Flexibacter)
rationale: The substrate is the C4 gem-diol intermediate of carotenoid ketolation, so the catalyst is most plausibly the single-polypeptide di-iron CrtW-type 4-ketolase (one oxygenase active site; its action at both C4 and C4' is substrate reuse, not a second activity), or the collapse is spontaneous. I could not confirm an enzyme assignment for MetaCyc RXN-19182 because biocyc.org was unreachable, so the identification is inferred from the chemistry.
direction_note: Dehydration of a gem-diol to the ketone is essentially irreversible in the written direction, which supports ModelSEED's '>' over the LLM's '<'.

organism_context: Rhodococcus, Geobacillus pallidus, Ensifer and other nitrile-utilising bacteria
rationale: Butanamide / butyronitrile + H2O is exactly EC 4.2.1.84, nitrile hydratase, whose IUBMB systematic name is 'aliphatic-amide hydro-lyase (nitrile-forming)'. NHase is an alpha-beta heterodimer of two separate polypeptides sharing one non-heme Fe(III) or Co(III) centre, i.e. a two-subunit complex with a single catalytic activity rather than a fused bifunctional chain.
direction_note: Nitrile hydratase physiologically hydrates the nitrile to the amide (butyronitrile + H2O -> butanamide), so the LLM's '<' is the biological direction; ModelSEED's '>' merely inherits the IUBMB nitrile-forming systematic name.

organism_context: Rhodobacter sphaeroides/capsulatus, Chlorobaculum tepidum and other (bacterio)chlorophyll producers
rationale: EC 4.2.1.165 assigns precisely this reaction (Rhea 15069 / KEGG R09059) to BchF, a small single-polypeptide membrane hydro-lyase; hydration and dehydration are the two directions of one reversible activity, and the apparent C3-1 epimerisation reported in vitro is the same chemistry run twice, not a second activity.
direction_note: BchF's biosynthetic role is the hydration (chlorophyllide a -> 3-(1-hydroxyethyl)chlorophyllide a), i.e. the LLM's '<'; in vitro, however, the enzyme readily runs the written dehydration and the vinyl form is recovered as the major species, which is exactly why the thermodynamic call ('>') and the pathway call ('<') disagree here.

organism_context: Rhodobacter spp. and Chlorobaculum tepidum bacteriochlorophyll a biosynthesis
rationale: This is the second reaction explicitly listed under EC 4.2.1.165 (Rhea 48772 / KEGG R09054): BchF acting on the bacteriochlorophyllide-level substrate. BchF is one polypeptide with a single hydro-lyase active site that accepts both the chlorophyllide and bacteriochlorophyllide series, which is substrate breadth rather than bifunctionality.
direction_note: The biosynthetic direction is hydration of the C3-vinyl group (the LLM's '<'), since the downstream BchC dehydrogenase pulls the 1-hydroxyethyl intermediate onward to the 3-acetyl group; the written dehydration ('>') is the in vitro reverse reaction.

enzyme_name: dicarboxylyl-CoA (adipyl-CoA) dehydrogenase, DcaA-type acyl-CoA dehydrogenase; a trans-2-enoyl-CoA reductase in the reductive sense
organism_context: Acinetobacter sp. ADP1 dca dicarboxylate beta-oxidation; engineered reverse beta-oxidation in Corynebacterium glutamicum / E. coli
rationale: The adipyl-CoA / trans-2,3-dehydroadipyl-CoA couple is handled in native dicarboxylate beta-oxidation by the standalone acyl-CoA dehydrogenase DcaA, a homotetrameric flavoprotein with a single dehydrogenase activity, and in engineered reverse beta-oxidation by a standalone trans-2-enoyl-CoA reductase. I could not resolve MetaCyc RXN-22975 itself (biocyc.org unreachable), so the protein assignment is inferred from the chemistry and pathway context.
direction_note: In native catabolism the flavoenzyme runs oxidatively (adipyl-CoA -> trans-2,3-dehydroadipyl-CoA), the LLM's '<'; the reductive sense written here is the reverse-beta-oxidation step and in practice requires a dedicated NAD(P)H-dependent trans-2-enoyl-CoA reductase rather than the dehydrogenase itself.

enzyme_name: succinate dehydrogenase / succinate:ubiquinone oxidoreductase (respiratory complex II)
organism_context: Saccharomyces cerevisiae and other fungi, where ubiquinone-6 is the native quinone
rationale: Complex II is a four-subunit membrane complex (FAD flavoprotein Sdh1/SdhA, iron-sulfur Sdh2/SdhB, membrane anchors Sdh3/Sdh4); per the protocol a multi-subunit complex is not bifunctional, and the catalytic flavoprotein subunit carries only the succinate/fumarate oxidoreductase activity. Called from established respiratory-chain biochemistry rather than a new literature search.
direction_note: The record is named 'fumarate reduction' but written as succinate oxidation; with ubiquinone-6 (Em' about +100 mV) the favoured direction is succinate -> fumarate ('>'), whereas fumarate reduction in vivo requires a low-potential quinone (menaquinone/rhodoquinone) and a distinct Frd-type enzyme, so the record's misleading name is the likely source of the LLM's '<'.

organism_context: Pseudomonas spp. (Yamada & Jakoby 1959, never sequenced); the tautomerase-superfamily protein Cg10062 of Corynebacterium glutamicum performs the same propiolate hydration
rationale: EC 4.2.1.71 was merged into EC 4.2.1.27, and the activity was only ever characterised as a purified pseudomonad hydratase with no gene or sequence, so its domain organisation is genuinely unknown. The closest molecularly defined catalyst for this chemistry, Cg10062, is a single-domain tautomerase-superfamily protein whose additional dehalogenase/decarboxylase chemistry is active-site promiscuity rather than a second fused domain.
direction_note: IUBMB states the reaction is effectively irreversible toward malonate semialdehyde: the enzyme hydrates propynoate to 3-hydroxypropenoate, which then tautomerises away, so the LLM's '<' is the real direction and ModelSEED's '>' (dehydration) runs against a tautomerisation-driven sink.

enzyme_name: unassigned; Neu5Ac2en is normally a sialidase (exo-/intramolecular trans-sialidase) elimination product rather than the product of a free-N-acetylneuraminate dehydratase
rationale: MetaCyc RXN0-7368 could not be resolved (biocyc.org unreachable) and the reaction carries no EC, KEGG or Rhea cross-reference. 2-deoxy-2,3-dehydro-Neu5Ac is generated as an elimination product by sialidases acting on sialosides, and no dedicated dehydratase acting on free N-acetylneuraminate is established, so neither the protein nor its domain organisation can be stated.
direction_note: No enzyme is known to hydrate Neu5Ac2en back to free Neu5Ac in vivo, so the written dehydration sense (ModelSEED's '>') is the only one with biochemical precedent.

enzyme_name: cob(II)alamin reductase activity - no dedicated enzyme established; PduS is the one protein claimed for the job
organism_context: Salmonella enterica pdu microcompartment (PduS); otherwise free dihydroflavins and non-specific reduced flavoproteins
rationale: IUBMB deleted EC 1.16.1.4 in 2021 precisely because no specific enzyme catalysing this reduction had been identified and cob(II)alamin is efficiently reduced by free dihydroflavins and non-specific flavoproteins. The one protein claimed for it, PduS, was reported as a bifunctional cobalamin reductase (cob(III)->cob(II) plus cob(II)->cob(I)), so the functionality call swings entirely on which assignment one accepts - an honest 'unknown'.
direction_note: Reducing cob(II)alamin with NADH is strongly uphill (cob(II)/cob(I) Em' about -610 mV versus -320 mV for NAD+/NADH), so the thermodynamic call favours the LLM's '>' (cob(I) oxidation); the ModelSEED direction only runs in vivo because the cob(I)alamin is immediately captured by an ATP:cob(I)alamin adenosyltransferase (PduO/CobA).

enzyme_name: hydrogen cyanide synthase (glycine dehydrogenase, HCN-forming), HcnABC
organism_context: Pseudomonas fluorescens CHA0, P. aeruginosa and other cyanogenic pseudomonads
rationale: The only established biochemistry linking glycine and HCN is HCN synthase, a membrane-bound flavoenzyme encoded as three separate polypeptides (HcnA/HcnB/HcnC, related to glycine and sarcosine oxidases); per the protocol a multi-subunit complex is not bifunctional, and the assembly carries a single oxidative-decarboxylation activity. The ModelSEED record is an unbalanced, cofactor-stripped stub with no xrefs, hence medium rather than high confidence.
direction_note: HCN synthase performs an irreversible four-electron oxidative decarboxylation of glycine to HCN + CO2, so the LLM's '>' (glycine -> HCN) is the biological direction and ModelSEED's '<' is chemically backwards.

organism_context: Methylobacterium extorquens DM4 (METDI2656), Hyphomicrobium sp. DM2/MC8b, Methylorubrum spp.
rationale: EC 4.5.1.3 is DcmA, a glutathione-dependent theta-class GST homologue that works as a homo-oligomer of one ~33 kDa chain with a single GSH-conjugating/dehalogenating active site. No second catalytic activity is reported for it.
direction_note: The reaction is a GSH-mediated hydrolytic dehalogenation releasing two chlorides and is irreversible toward formaldehyde, so the LLM's '>' (dichloromethane + H2O -> formaldehyde + 2 HCl) is the only direction the enzyme runs; ModelSEED's '<' would require condensing formaldehyde with chloride.

distinct_activities: oxidative deamination of L-phenylalanine to phenylpyruvate + NH3 + H2O2 (L-amino-acid oxidase, EC 1.4.3.2)
oxygenative decarboxylation of L-phenylalanine to 2-phenylacetamide + CO2 (phenylalanine 2-monooxygenase, EC 1.13.12.9)
organism_context: Pseudomonas sp. P-501; homodimer of two identical 68 kDa FAD-containing subunits
rationale: The enzyme that actually makes 2-phenylacetamide from L-phenylalanine is the Pseudomonas P-501 flavoprotein, which simultaneously runs an oxidase (deaminating) and a genuine monooxygenase (decarboxylating - 18O from O2 is incorporated into the amide carbonyl) with different pH and temperature optima on the same 68 kDa chain. ModelSEED's EC 1.11.1.7 'peroxidase, putative' label is a legacy mis-assignment (KEGG R00698 now points to a catalase-peroxidase, itself also bifunctional), which is why confidence is medium rather than high.
direction_note: Both activities consume O2 irreversibly and release CO2, so the reaction can only run L-phenylalanine -> 2-phenylacetamide (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's '<' is an artefact of a stub record from which O2 and CO2 were stripped.

enzyme_name: glycerol-3-phosphate dehydrogenase, FAD/quinone-linked (GlpD; anaerobic GlpABC; mitochondrial GPD2)
organism_context: E. coli aerobic GlpD (single chain) and anaerobic GlpABC (three subunits, KEGG K00111/K00112/K00113); mitochondrial GPD2
rationale: Aerobic GlpD and mitochondrial GPD2 are single-polypeptide FAD flavoenzymes with one dehydrogenase active site; GPD2's EF-hand calcium-binding module is regulatory, not catalytic, so it does not count as a second activity. The anaerobic E. coli isozyme GlpABC is a three-subunit complex, which per the protocol still scores monofunctional for the catalytic GlpA subunit.
direction_note: The FAD/quinone-linked enzyme is physiologically unidirectional, oxidising glycerol-3-phosphate and passing electrons into the quinone pool (the LLM's '>'); the reverse reaction (DHAP -> G3P) is carried out in vivo by the separate NAD(H)-linked enzyme GpsA/GPD1, so ModelSEED's '<' assigns a different enzyme's direction to this one.

organism_context: Chicken/sauropsid embryo yolk sac; cysteine lyase arose in early amniotes as a paralogue of cystathionine beta-synthase
rationale: EC 4.4.1.10 is a pyridoxal-phosphate beta-replacement enzyme, and the sauropsid cysteine lyase is a single-domain CBS paralogue with one beta-replacement active site. Its ability to substitute other thiols for sulfite (forming lanthionine) is substrate promiscuity at that one site, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: This is the committed, effectively irreversible beta-replacement step of embryonic taurine biosynthesis (L-cysteine + sulfite -> L-cysteate + H2S), i.e. the LLM's '>'; ModelSEED's '<' would require H2S to displace a sulfonate, which PLP beta-replacement chemistry cannot do.

enzyme_name: propionyl-CoA dehydrogenase / acryloyl-CoA reductase (PCD, in complex with electron-transferring flavoprotein)
organism_context: Clostridium propionicum acrylate pathway (PCD-EtfAB complex); the oxidative direction is also run by ordinary acyl-CoA dehydrogenases
rationale: The characterised catalyst for the acrylyl-CoA/propionyl-CoA couple at EC 1.3.99.3 is an enzyme complex of a propionyl-CoA dehydrogenase chain plus a separate electron-transferring flavoprotein (EtfA/EtfB) - per the protocol a multi-subunit assembly, not a fused bifunctional chain. The dehydrogenase chain itself carries only the acyl-CoA dehydrogenase / enoyl-CoA reductase activity.
direction_note: Both directions are physiological in different organisms: acyl-CoA dehydrogenases oxidise propionyl-CoA in beta-alanine/propionate catabolism (the LLM's '>'), while in Clostridium propionicum the same PCD-Etf complex runs reductively (acrylyl-CoA -> propionyl-CoA, ModelSEED's '<') as the electron-bifurcating step of the acrylate fermentation - a genuine organism-dependent direction conflict.

organism_context: Short-chain fatty acid-grown bacteria studied by Reeves and Ajl; the protein was never sequenced
rationale: The stub is EC 2.3.3.11 (propanoyl-CoA + glyoxylate + H2O -> (R)-2-hydroxyglutarate + CoA, KEGG R00932) with CoA and water stripped out. Wegener, Reeves and Ajl showed by differential heat inactivation and non-constant activity ratios that alpha-hydroxyglutarate synthase is a separate protein from malate synthase and the other glyoxylate-condensing enzymes, explicitly ruling out a single broad-specificity multifunctional condensing enzyme.
direction_note: The condensation is driven by hydrolysis of the propanoyl-CoA thioester and is effectively irreversible toward 2-hydroxyglutarate (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's '<' would require regenerating a CoA thioester from a free acid, which this acyltransferase cannot do.

distinct_activities: anthranilate adenylation (A domain; the former EC 2.7.7.55 anthranilate adenylyltransferase)
peptide bond formation / cyclization (condensation domain; overall EC 6.3.2.40)
organism_context: Penicillium cyclopium and related benzodiazepine-alkaloid-producing fungi
rationale: IUBMB deleted EC 2.7.7.55 (anthranilate adenylyltransferase) in 2013 on the grounds that the activity is a partial reaction of EC 6.3.2.40, cyclopeptine synthase - a non-ribosomal peptide synthetase whose single polypeptide carries two adenylation domains, carrier domains, an N-methyltransferase domain and a condensation/cyclization domain. The free adenylate shown here is an enzyme-bound intermediate of that megasynthetase, not the product of a standalone transferase.
direction_note: The adenylation half-reaction is reversible in isolation but is pulled forward in vivo by pyrophosphatase and by immediate transfer of the anthraniloyl group onto the NRPS carrier domain, so the physiological sense is ATP + anthranilate -> anthraniloyl-AMP + PPi (the LLM's '>').

enzyme_name: aldose reductase (alditol:NAD(P)+ 1-oxidoreductase, AKR1B1); galactitol dehydrogenase in bacteria
organism_context: Mammalian lens, nerve and kidney aldose reductase; EC 1.1.1.21 is a broad-specificity aldo-keto reductase family
rationale: EC 1.1.1.21 enzymes are single-domain (beta/alpha)8 aldo-keto reductases with one NAD(P)-dependent carbonyl-reduction active site; the 'wide specificity' noted by IUBMB is promiscuity at that site, not a second catalytic activity.
direction_note: Aldose reductase runs essentially irreversibly in the reductive sense (galactose + NAD(P)H -> galactitol, the basis of galactitol accumulation and cataract in galactosemia), matching the LLM's '>'; note that the ModelSEED record is redox-mangled - NAD+ sits on the galactose side and NADH on the galactitol side, the opposite of the EC equation - so neither stored direction is trustworthy as written.

enzyme_name: very-long-chain / long-chain acyl-CoA dehydrogenase (ACADVL, ACADL); peroxisomal acyl-CoA oxidase (ACOX1) for the EC 1.3.3.6 variant
organism_context: Mitochondrial VLCAD (membrane-bound homodimer) and peroxisomal acyl-CoA oxidase (homodimer); bacterial FadE
rationale: KEGG R01279 maps to EC 1.3.8.9/1.3.8.8/1.3.3.6, and both VLCAD and acyl-CoA oxidase are single-activity FAD flavoproteins that perform only the alpha,beta-dehydrogenation. The genuinely multifunctional beta-oxidation enzymes (peroxisomal MFE, mitochondrial trifunctional protein) act at the later hydratase/dehydrogenase/thiolase steps, not at this one.
direction_note: The flavoenzyme is effectively irreversible toward the 2-enoyl-CoA because electrons are passed on to ETF/quinone (or to O2 for acyl-CoA oxidase), so the LLM's '>' is the physiological direction; the reductive '<' sense is carried out in vivo by a different enzyme class (NADPH-dependent trans-2-enoyl-CoA reductase).

enzyme_name: 4-chlorobenzoyl-CoA dehalogenase (FcbB), the catalytic component of the three-enzyme 4-chlorobenzoate dehalogenase system
organism_context: Pseudomonas sp. strain CBS-3, Arthrobacter sp. 4-CB1 and TM-1
rationale: EC 3.8.1.6 ('4-chlorobenzoate dehalogenase') was deleted as identical to EC 3.8.1.7, and the overall activity was resolved into three separate polypeptides - a CoA ligase (FcbA), the crotonase-superfamily dehalogenase (FcbB) and a thioesterase (FcbC). Per the protocol a multi-enzyme system is not bifunctional, and FcbB itself is a homotrimer carrying the single dehalogenation activity.
direction_note: Hydrolytic aromatic dehalogenation via a Meisenheimer/aryl-enzyme intermediate is irreversible toward 4-hydroxybenzoate (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's '<' would require chloride to displace a phenolate, which does not occur, and the stripped record is also missing the ATP/CoA that the real three-step system consumes.

organism_context: E. coli / Salmonella PrpE, mammalian ACSS3; ANL (acyl-CoA synthetase/NRPS-adenylation/luciferase) superfamily
rationale: KEGG notes that R01354 is the first of a two-step reaction of EC 6.2.1.17/6.2.1.1. Acyl-adenylate formation and thioesterification are two half-reactions of a single ANL-superfamily ligase active site operating by domain alternation, not two distinct catalytic activities, so the enzyme is monofunctional.
direction_note: The adenylation half-reaction is close to isoenergetic on its own and is pulled forward in vivo by inorganic pyrophosphatase and by the immediate second half-reaction with CoA, so the physiological sense is ATP + propionate -> propionyl-AMP + PPi (the LLM's '>'); ModelSEED's '<' reflects the unfavourable standard free energy of the isolated half-reaction rather than pathway flux.
